question.EN: Which of the following is considered the most fundamental and defining characteristic of all living organisms, including single isolated cells outside a living system?
question.HI: Which of the following is considered the most fundamental and defining characteristic of all living organisms, including single isolated cells outside a living system?

explanation.EN: Metabolism (the sum total of all chemical reactions occurring in the body) is the defining feature of life. Isolated metabolic reactions can even be demonstrated outside the body in a cell-free system, but such a system is not considered 'living'.
explanation.HI: Metabolism (the sum total of all chemical reactions occurring in the body) is the defining feature of life. Isolated metabolic reactions can even be demonstrated outside the body in a cell-free system, but such a system is not considered 'living'.

question.EN: Why is reproduction NOT considered a defining property applicable to every individual organism?
question.HI: Why is reproduction NOT considered a defining property applicable to every individual organism?

EN: Because sterile worker bees, mules, and infertile human couples do not reproduce yet are alive
Because reproduction only occurs in unicellular organisms
Because reproduction is a purely chemical process
Because only plants reproduce, not animals
HI: Because sterile worker bees, mules, and infertile human couples do not reproduce yet are alive
Because reproduction only occurs in unicellular organisms
Because reproduction is a purely chemical process
Because only plants reproduce, not animals

explanation.EN: Many individual organisms such as mules, worker bees, and infertile couples do not reproduce during their lifetime, so reproduction cannot be used as a defining feature for every living individual, even though it is a characteristic of populations of organisms.
explanation.HI: Many individual organisms such as mules, worker bees, and infertile couples do not reproduce during their lifetime, so reproduction cannot be used as a defining feature for every living individual, even though it is a characteristic of populations of organisms.

question.EN: A crystal placed in a saturated solution increases in mass. How does this growth fundamentally differ from growth in a living organism?
question.HI: A crystal placed in a saturated solution increases in mass. How does this growth fundamentally differ from growth in a living organism?

EN: Crystal growth occurs by accumulation of material on the surface (extrinsic), while growth in most living organisms occurs from inside (intrinsic), by an increase in cell number or cell size
Crystal growth is intrinsic, organismal growth is extrinsic
Crystals grow faster than living organisms
There is no real difference between the two
HI: Crystal growth occurs by accumulation of material on the surface (extrinsic), while growth in most living organisms occurs from inside (intrinsic), by an increase in cell number or cell size
Crystal growth is intrinsic, organismal growth is extrinsic
Crystals grow faster than living organisms
There is no real difference between the two

explanation.EN: Growth in non-living objects like crystals is purely extrinsic, by simple accumulation of material on the surface. In living organisms, growth is intrinsic, arising from an increase in the number of cells or the size of cells within the organism.
explanation.HI: Growth in non-living objects like crystals is purely extrinsic, by simple accumulation of material on the surface. In living organisms, growth is intrinsic, arising from an increase in the number of cells or the size of cells within the organism.

question.EN: Unicellular organisms such as bacteria grow mainly by:

explanation.HI: In unicellular organisms, growth is generally seen as an increase in the volume of the single cell, whereas in multicellular organisms, growth is mainly due to an increase in cell number.

question.EN:
Consider the following statements about characteristics of life:
(i) Growth is an increase in mass and number of cells.
(ii) Reproduction is seen in every individual organism without exception.
(iii) Metabolism can be demonstrated in a cell-free system.
(iv) Consciousness means sensing the environment and responding to stimuli.
How many of the above statements are correct?
question.HI:
Consider the following statements about characteristics of life:
(i) Growth is an increase in mass and number of cells.
(ii) Reproduction is seen in every individual organism without exception.
(iii) Metabolism can be demonstrated in a cell-free system.
(iv) Consciousness means sensing the environment and responding to stimuli.
How many of the above statements are correct?

explanation.EN: Statements (i), (iii), and (iv) are correct. Statement (ii) is incorrect because reproduction is not seen in every individual (e.g., mules, sterile worker bees), so only three statements are correct.
explanation.HI: Statements (i), (iii), and (iv) are correct. Statement (ii) is incorrect because reproduction is not seen in every individual (e.g., mules, sterile worker bees), so only three statements are correct.
